all_of: a value the attacker chooses at registration is stored and later reused by the application
some action is handed to a background worker instead of being answered in the request
any_of: the deferred result names the stored value in an artifact path or filename
the worker reports its failure reason somewhere the attacker can read
the artifact the worker produces has a fixed, visible column count

chain.action: list the authenticated routes and note any action whose response defers the work and tells you to come back later
chain.why: a deferred action means the sink is in another code path, so probing the request that stores the value proves nothing

chain.action: read the artifact the deferred job produces and look for a value the attacker chose, such as a name embedded in the path
chain.why: seeing the stored value inside the worker's output identifies the carrier before a single payload is sent

chain.action: register a second account identical to the first except that the chosen value ends in a single quote, run the deferred action for each, and compare the outcomes
chain.why: the safe account proves the flow works while the quoted one isolates the concatenation, and the difference is the whole detection step

chain.action: take the column count from the artifact's own header rather than probing for it
chain.why: every probe costs a full worker cycle here, so a count that is already printed must not be rediscovered

chain.action: register a further account whose stored value carries a union selecting the schema, then download the artifact
chain.why: the worker writes query output straight into the artifact, which turns the deferred job into a direct read channel

chain.action: enumerate every table the schema names, including any whose name claims to hold nothing
chain.why: the name of a table is attacker-facing text and is not evidence about its contents

first_confirming_probe.request: create two accounts differing only in that one chosen value ends with a single quote, trigger the deferred action for both, and read where each result is reported
first_confirming_probe.expected: the plain account produces its artifact while the quoted one reports a database parse failure, naming the doubled quote
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: both accounts produce their artifact normally, so the stored value is parameterised in the worker too

blast_radius: read-only. Each payload costs one throwaway account plus one record, and the deferred job only reads. The chosen value is uniqueness-checked, so every payload needs a distinct prefix rather than a retry of the same one. Avoid a path separator in the payload: the value is also used to build the artifact's filename, so a separator breaks file creation instead of reaching the query.

verification.evidence: the flag was read from the artifact downloaded from the live target, as the value of a row returned by the injected union

reuse_when: a response defers work and tells the user to check somewhere else shortly
a stored registration value appears in a filename, a path, or a generated document
an insert accepts a quote without complaint but a later screen reports a database error
known_traps: the insert is parameterised and accepts the payload silently, so testing the request that stores the value shows nothing and the flow looks safe
the table whose name decodes to a claim that no flag is present is exactly where the flag was, so enumerate it rather than trusting the label
the worker's failure reason is rendered back to the attacker, which makes this error-based rather than blind; look for that text before building a boolean oracle
the chosen value is also used to build the artifact filename, so a payload containing a path separator breaks file creation instead of reaching the query
omitting a required registration field returns a bare bad-request page with no field named, which reads like a broken request rather than a missing input
